_note: Selection scoring (Block 9 §11), weights fixed BEFORE scoring and not revisited after seeing which family won. Scores are this project's own qualitative-to-0-10 judgment calls, disclosed as such — not an external benchmark, and not a substitute for the actual pre-registered backtest that would follow a review of this ranking.
weightJustification: Adopted the brief's own example weights (§11) unchanged. Academic evidence + economic rationale + data quality (50 combined) dominate deliberately, consistent with this project's established culture (Blocks 4/4.5/5/8/8.2/8.3/8.4) of rejecting anything that can't survive independent scrutiny before it can survive a backtest. RS3M diversification (15) is weighted above parameter simplicity and tail-risk SCORE specifically because tail risk is handled as a hard GATE (see below), not only a scoring input — a family that fails the gate is excluded regardless of its total score, so its 5-point weight in the additive score is intentionally small.
tailRiskGate: Per §16, no family advances on score alone if it relies on hidden short-vol/leverage/negative-skew exposure without a defined-risk structure. Family E (Volatility Risk Premium) is the only Top-5 entry that would fail this gate in its NAIVE form (unhedged short volatility) — it only clears the gate because its pre-registration (see docs/BLOCK9_STRATEGY2_PREREGISTRATION.md) mandates a defined-risk implementation (put spread / covered short-vol-ETP position with a hard stop) as a condition of testing, not an optional refinement.
rankingCaveat: M (89) and F (88) score close behind D (91), and both narrowly ahead of C and E on a total-points basis; the published Top-5 order additionally weighs M's disclosed HIGH decay risk and E's tail-risk gate qualitatively, which the additive score does not fully capture — see the discovery report's per-family write-up for the qualitative tie-breakers. All five are being pre-registered together in this round regardless of internal order; the ranking is for prioritization within the 20-configuration budget (§19), not a cutoff that drops #4/#5.
